resplendent

/rih-SPLEN-duhnt/ - the stress falls on SPLEN · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Resplendent means dazzlingly splendid; gloriously bright.

The peacock fanned its tail and stood resplendent, a hundred green-gold eyes catching the sun.

Example

The tall ship came up the channel for the festival resplendent: full sail set, forty signal flags snapping from her rigging, brass rails flashing, her bow carvings freshly leafed in gold. Traffic stopped on the bluff road. Children who had never cared about boats pointed and yelled. She was, for one morning, the only thing worth looking at on that water.

Resplendent is the exact word for the ship that morning, because it means dazzlingly splendid, gloriously bright — light and majesty arriving together. Dazzling alone could describe a welder's arc; resplendent insists the eye is overwhelmed and honored at once.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

dazzling: Dazzling is light-first — anything bright enough can dazzle, from a welder's arc to headlights on high beam, and the word says nothing about grandeur. Resplendent asks for more: the eye must be overwhelmed and honored at once, with majesty riding on the light.

magnificent: Magnificent means grand — by size, cost, or sheer ambition — and it needs no shine at all. Resplendent is narrower: reserved for visual glory, where light and majesty arrive together, so a thing must actually blaze before resplendent fits it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

drab: dull, colorless, beneath notice

dingy: grimy and dim with wear

Where it sits · how much grandeur the shine takes on

bright → gleaming → resplendent

bright vs. resplendent: Bright is plain light, far below resplendent — a hallway bulb manages bright, with no majesty anywhere in it.

gleaming vs. resplendent: Gleaming goes further than bright — surfaces polished until they flash — but it stops short of resplendent, which adds majesty to the shine: a whole presence lit up in glory.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-: thoroughly (an intensifier)

Root — splend-: to shine (Latin splendere)

Suffix — -ent: in a state of

Put it together: Re- (here an intensifier: thoroughly, out) + splend- (to shine) + -ent = shining out through and through. Nothing shines 'again' in this word — Latin resplendere used re- the way we use 'utterly.' Resplendent is splendid pushed to its ceiling: light plus majesty, glory you can see.

Use the root in a new word: splendid: Reviewers called the aurora splendid, and crowds drove north all winter to see it.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Resplendent is reserved for visual glory — light plus majesty. Dazzling can describe any bright thing and magnificent any grand one; resplendent insists the eye is overwhelmed and honored at once, which is why it gravitates to ceremonies, plumage, treasure, and skies. No unit-mate competes for its lane; just remember the re- is an intensifier, not 'again' — the word promises shining through and through, never shining twice.
